localChanges: The Civilopedia's city improvement pages now say what each building does, such as a Library's +50% science, a Temple's content citizens and a Barracks' Veterans, along with its upkeep. The wording comes from the game's own rules, so it always matches how the game plays (#1196).

log: The corruption rule describes the Palace with core-rule's Description. Requires core-rule 0.1.10.
Each rule describes its row of the exported contentImprovements table with core-rule's Description; the Temple's Mysticism row says it makes one more. Requires core-rule 0.1.10.

Each improvement's rules describe what they do (yields, upkeep, the Granary, the Aqueduct, pollution, Mass Transit and the Barracks' Veterans) with core-rule's Description, from the same tables the rules use. Requires core-rule 0.1.10.

With its rule sets on, the rules that take Civ1's place describe what they do as Civ1's do: pollution in every city says Mass Transit stops the population polluting, and SDI Defense sparing cities says the city loses no people. Requires core-rule 0.1.10 and civ1-city-improvement 0.1.14.
The strength and detonation rules describe City Walls' multiplier (exported as cityWallsMultiplier) and SDI Defense with core-rule's Description. Requires core-rule 0.1.10.

A Description holds effect descriptions, { type, ...fields }, given to a rule beside its criteria and effect and read with rule.descriptions(). A Description from another copy of this package is recognised by its shape, and an item a rule can't take now throws rather than becoming its priority.
Only a rule given a Description has the _descriptions field, so a rule reachable from saved state (a unit's _busy) is saved as it was before 0.1.10 (civ-clone/web-renderer#1196).
